validation_notes: In the last ~4 weeks of the chart (mid-July to end), price highs are stepping down (~79 -> 77 -> 75 -> 74) while the lows are holding a fairly flat floor around 71-73. This looks more like a descending triangle (flat support, falling resistance) than a true symmetric wedge, since the lower boundary isn't clearly rising - it's roughly horizontal. There are at least 3 touches on the upper declining line and 3-4 touches on the flat lower support, so the compression is real, but the lower trendline doesn't show the rising-low structure needed for a symmetric or ascending pattern. Price is still contained within the range near the apex, so the pattern is unresolved rather than broken out. I'd relabel the algorithm's 'Symmetric' call as 'Descending' based on the flatness of the support line, though the overall convergence/compression observation is valid.
